unit.title: Preterite vs imperfect
unit.subtitle: Choosing the right past tense: the moment vs the backdrop

grammar.title: Two pasts, one story
grammar.intro: Spanish has two past tenses and they do different jobs. The preterite reports a completed action — something that happened and finished. The imperfect paints the background: descriptions, habits, and actions in progress. The magic is how they work together: the imperfect sets the scene, and the preterite is what suddenly happens.

sections.heading: Preterite = a finished moment
sections.body: Use the preterite for a single, completed action — with a clear start or end. It's the verb that moves the story forward:

ex.en: Yesterday I ate at a restaurant.

sections.heading: Imperfect = the ongoing backdrop
sections.body: Use the imperfect for descriptions, habits, and actions in progress — no clear end point. Cue words like mientras and siempre point here:

ex.en: While I ate, I listened to music.
As a child I always played outside.

sections.heading: The two together: interruption
sections.body: Very often one sentence uses both: the imperfect gives the ongoing background, and the preterite is the action that interrupts it. English does this with “was …-ing … when …”:

ex.en: I was eating when you called.
I was sleeping when the alarm went off.

takeaways: Preterite = a completed, finished action; imperfect = background, description, habit.
Cues for preterite: de repente, ayer, anoche, un día.
Cues for imperfect: mientras, siempre, todos los días, normalmente.
Together: imperfect (was …-ing) + preterite interruption. “Comía cuando llamaste.”

mistakes.w: La casa fue grande y bonita.
mistakes.r: La casa era grande y bonita.
mistakes.why: A description of how something was uses the imperfect: era, not the preterite fue.

mistakes.w: Ayer comía en un restaurante nuevo.
mistakes.r: Ayer comí en un restaurante nuevo.
mistakes.why: 'Ayer' points to one finished action, so use the preterite: comí.
The interrupting event is a single finished action → preterite: sonó.

exercises.no: “De repente” signals a sudden finished action → preterite: “sonó”.
